Transgender people have the right to medical privacy. According to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), medical providers and insurance companies are prohibited from disclosing any personal medical information including a person's transgender status. HIPAA also allows transgender people to access and receive a copy of their medical records from health care facilities.

In terms of insurance coverage, it can be difficult for transgender people to find coverage for their medical needs. Even though there is medical consensus that hormone therapy and sex reassignment surgery (SRS) are medically necessary treatments for many transgender people, some insurance companies still refuse to cover them. This can make it difficult for transgender people to access the medical care they need to live healthy and fulfilling lives.
